t: The Odyssey grew out of an oral tradition over hundreds of years, and whether Homer lived, and when, is still debated.
Its story of Odysseus's return to Ithaca turns on homecoming, wandering, guest-friendship, testing and omens, and gives women and slaves larger roles than most ancient literature.
It was a school text across the Greek and Roman worlds and Byzantium, and its retellings run from Dante and Joyce to modern novels and films.
dyk: Penelope tests the returned Odysseus by asking to have their bed moved; only he knows it cannot be, because he carved it from the trunk of a living olive tree.
ev: The Odyssey is composed in Homeric Greek as part of a long oral tradition
The Homeric poems gain a canonical place in Athens, probably performed at the Panathenaia festival
Alexandrian scholars such as Aristarchus of Samothrace study and edit the text
Nicholas Sigeros provides Petrarch with manuscripts of the Iliad and the Odyssey
Demetrios Chalkokondyles produces the first printed edition, printed in Milan
George Chapman's translations of both epics are published together, the first complete Odyssey in English
James Joyce publishes Ulysses, a reworking of the Odyssey set in Dublin

f.made: Attributed to Homer, whose life and authorship are debated; most scholars hold that it grew out of a long oral tradition of Greek poets and was performed by singers (aoidoi) and rhapsodes
f.form: An epic poem in Homeric Greek of 12109 lines in dactylic hexameter, divided into 24 books
f.where: The Greek text survives through ancient and Byzantine scholarship; the first printed edition appeared in Milan in 1488
f.known: Odysseus's homecoming (nostos); the Cyclops Polyphemus and the name Nobody; Penelope's weaving and faithfulness; the Sirens, Scylla and Charybdis; guest-friendship (xenia); the contest of the bow
